newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan under pressure to rise again-paper.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan under pressure to rise again-paper.

text.p: The Chinese yuan is under pressure to rise again in 1997 for the fourth consecutive year due to China's surging foreign exchange reserves and foreign trade surplus, the Business News said on Thursday.

"In 1997, foreign exchange supply will continue to exceed demand, as it has in the past three years," the newspaper quoted an unnamed official with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange as saying.
"The Chinese yuan will face pressure to rise further this year after three years of consecutive rises," he said.
The yuan rose 0.3 percent in 1996 after a rise of 2.9 percent in 1994 and 1.5 percent in 1995, the newspaper said, but did not forecast a range of possible rises for 1997.

By the end of 1996, China's foreign exchange reserves hit a record high of $105 billion yuan, about five times figure at the end of 1993 and an increase of $31.5 billion yuan against the end of 1995, the newspaper quoted the official as saying.
In 1996, China had a foreign trade surplus of $12 billion and it is expected to continue to score a surplus this year, the official was quoted as saying.
